title: Gootloader Malware Using SEO Poisoning and Compromised Websites to Gain Initial Access
claim: The FBI linked Gootloader infections from compromised websites and poisoned search results to downstream ransomware. As of October 2026, the FBI had identified more than 1,000 infected WordPress sites and 216 domains controlled by the operator.
location: FLASH CC-111626-MW, Summary

title: Shutting the Door on the XCPE Botnet
claim: Google Threat Intelligence Group reported that Google and its partners disrupted a backdoor that had enrolled more than 1.3 million set-top boxes in the XCPE botnet.
location: Introduction

title: Virtualization security: attack layers and misconfiguration impact
claim: Kaspersky investigated ransomware incidents in ESXi and Proxmox environments where excessive privilege, exposed management access and poor credential handling increased the impact. Its guidance calls for dedicated monitoring identities, restricted management networks and protected logs and backups.
location: Introduction and remediation guidance

title: BengalSEO Part 1: Anatomy of the Operation
claim: The DFIR Report identified an SEO poisoning campaign in March 2026 that steered users toward tech support scams and malware. The researchers track the operation as BengalSEO and named its custom malware MayaBot.
location: Key Takeaways and Case Summary

title: CastleRAT Historical Bot Infection Special Report (Stolen Credentials)
claim: After the November Operation Endgame disruption, Shadowserver issued a CastleRAT notification report for network owners and national response teams. The public analysis reports about 2.5 million distinct affected website and account combinations.
location: Special Report and Data Analysis sections of the public announcement

title: An Active Intrusion Campaign Against Check Point Security Management Servers
claim: GreyNoise attributed activity against at least 22 organizations to the cluster it tracks as GT13. Its confirmed Check Point Security Management Server campaign activity spanned October 17 to November 2, 2026, and the report cites Check Point CVE-2026-16232.
location: Campaign Summary

title: Impersonating IT support: how threat actors turn a remote session into enterprise-wide access
claim: Microsoft observed PowerShell downloading an MSI after fraudulent remote support access.
location: Execution and MITRE ATT&CK sections

title: The global socket: how threat actors are weaponizing GSocket for stealthy C2
claim: Microsoft observed GSocket tooling on compromised Linux servers, including renamed relay binaries, cron persistence and connections to GSocket distribution infrastructure.
location: Advanced hunting queries and indicators sections
indicators: Public GSocket distribution domain. The service is dual-use.
Public GSocket distribution host. The service is dual-use.

title: High volume phishing campaign uses Microsoft 365 outage lures to target multiple industry sectors
claim: Microsoft reported downstream destinations and a redirect path in deceptive Microsoft 365 service-health messages. The report did not confirm credential submission.
location: Lure and redirect flow, MITRE ATT&CK, and indicators sections

title: From help desk impersonation to AD CS abuse: Investigating ESC1 and ESC8 intrusion paths
claim: Microsoft observed fraudulent Quick Assist support sessions followed by scripting and certificate-services abuse during the investigated intrusions.
location: Intrusion case studies and initial access sections

title: Threat actors use agentic AI tooling to find and abuse exposed secrets
claim: Microsoft observed ARTEX-associated use of exposed cloud credentials, service-principal sign-ins from a reported IP, rapid cloud discovery and attempted access to Azure Key Vault and other resources.
location: Credential abuse via Entra ID and indicators sections
indicators: IP observed in successful service principal sign-ins across multiple applications.

title: ARTEX abuse expands as cybercriminals target financial sector
claim: Microsoft reported Storm-3358 using ARTEX around financial-sector intrusions, including fast network probing, password abuse and infrastructure associated with remote access tooling.
location: Behavioral signals and indicators sections
indicators: Listed by Microsoft as an ARTEX server.
Listed by Microsoft as an ARTEX server.

title: Tracking AI adoption in North Korean threat actor tradecraft
claim: Microsoft documented North Korean actors adopting AI, identified Onyx Sleet and Pearl Sleet using ARTEX, and listed Defender detections for Jasper Sleet sign-ins and Sapphire Sleet-related ProcmacSteal payloads.
location: AI-assisted development, operational scaling and Microsoft Defender detections

title: AI-driven, large-scale nation-state campaign using ARTEX enables supply chain compromise
claim: Microsoft attributed application abuse, password spraying and cloud role or credential changes to Storm-0940, a China-state-aligned actor, in activity that included the ConnectWise Cloud Backup compromise.
location: Observed attack patterns, Sentinel queries and ATT&CK mapping
indicators: Microsoft associated this address with spraying and ConnectWise-related activity.
Included in the publisher's Sentinel pivots.

title: SCKit abuses ScreenConnect to deploy remote access and target technician sessions
claim: Microsoft documented unauthorized ScreenConnect sessions, scripting, scheduled tasks, Run keys and changes to Defender exclusions while investigating SCKit.
location: Investigation guidance and advanced hunting examples

title: The risks of device code authentication for AI coding agents
claim: Microsoft demonstrated in a lab that device code phishing can expose sessions used by coding agents, and noted earlier device-code phishing campaigns. The demonstration is distinct from observed incidents.
location: Research scope and mitigation guidance

title: Drupal core installer remote code execution advisory SA-CORE-2026-017
claim: The Drupal Security Team received a report of live exploitation starting November 19. The team identifies settings.php writability by the web server as a condition for some exploitation paths. The hunt infers a file-write signal from this condition.
location: Description and exploitation update

title: CTIR Gov technical recommendation 23/2026 for the Microsoft Outlook vulnerability
claim: Brazil's government incident response center documents unintended external authentication from affected Outlook clients and recommends monitoring unexpected outbound SMB and other authentication-related connections.
location: Sections 2 and 5(b–d), as updated November 16

title: GitLab critical patch release 19.4.2, 19.3.5 and 19.2.8
claim: GitLab Security publishes exploitation-attempt detections for vulnerable self-managed GitLab CE/EE. Its linked Onigmo guidance identifies compile-time crash frames together with regexp_matcher.rb as corroborating traces of the CI path.
location: Detecting CVE-2026-97229 Exploitation Attempts and linked Onigmo native worker crash detection

title: Volexity investigation of chained Ivanti Connect Secure exploitation
claim: Volexity recovered a masquerading packet sniffer and its credential-parsing companion script after compromise of an Ivanti Connect Secure appliance. Its October 29 update identifies CVE-2026-111357 as the privilege-escalation stage.
location: October 29 update, LDAP Packet Capture, and Ivanti Memory Analysis with Volexity Volcano

title: AWS WAF mitigations and managed rules for PHP2Shell
claim: AWS publishes PHP2Shell_BODY and PHP2Shell_BODY_Extended as managed WAF rules for request behavior associated with the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities. The rules have overlapping coverage.
location: Updates of October 22 and 23 and AWS WAF coverage table

title: Amazon Threat Intelligence investigation of a Cairn AI agent campaign
claim: Amazon Threat Intelligence observed a write to Python's sitecustomize.py on a compromised medical-imaging AI server and links to the Project MONAI advisory for the underlying file-write issue.
location: Zero-day discovery and the linked Project MONAI advisory in Actions taken by AWS

title: Optimizely Web Experimentation initial security incident report
claim: Optimizely reports edits to customer Project JavaScript following exploitation of a signup flaw. Its forensic investigation identified separate skimmer hosting and collection domains.
location: How the attack worked and section 10, Indicators of compromise
indicators: Skimmer campaign infrastructure named in Optimizely's investigation and shared with other activity.
Skimmer hosting identified in the Optimizely incident investigation.
Collection endpoint identified in the Optimizely incident investigation.

title: F6 investigation of Cisco Expressway CVE-2026-76466 exploitation
claim: F6 found Python packages staged in shared memory and numbered working directories under /mnt/harddisk/ on compromised Cisco Expressway appliances. The investigators report the naming pattern as a possible ARTEX link.
location: Post-compromise Python tooling and working-directory findings
